chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qazvini, known as Ibn Muqbara, narrated to us; he said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami informed us; he said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ahwal narrated to us; he said: Khalad al-Muqri narrated, from Qays, from Abu al-Husayn, from Yahya ibn Wathab, from Ibn Umar, who said:
There were two amulets upon al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), filled with fuzz from the wing of Gabriel (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What were the amulets of Imam al-Hasan and Imam al-Husayn made of?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt by linking their protective amulets directly to the Angel Gabriel, suggesting a tangible connection to divine revelation. In Shia tradition, this underscores the belief that the Imams possess unique spiritual authority and that their physical possessions can serve as vessels of barakah (blessing) and protection, rooted in the very presence of the Archangel.
